title: Unify TypeScript SDK stream consumers: AsyncIterator, Web Streams, and pull-based APIs
creator: Diego Ramos
description: Problem: TypeScript SDK currently exposes multiple ad-hoc streaming entry points (stream bridge, raw web ReadableStream, and async-iterator helpers). Consumers across Node/Deno/Browser and edge runtimes face friction around typing, backpressure, abort semantics, and retries. Goal: provide a single, well-typed consumer surface that interops seamlessly with AsyncIterator, WHATWG ReadableStream (Web Streams), and Node streams, while preserving retry semantics and graceful aborts. Deliver clear examples for Next.js Edge, Deno, and Node 18+/20+ runtimes.
acceptance_criteria: Library exports a StreamConsumerFactory<T> that can produce: AsyncIterable<T>, ReadableStream<T>, and NodeReadable (where available)
TypeScript types express event-level union (data | token | error | done) with narrow generics for payload vs control events
Backpressure respected: consumer produced via factory applies native backpressure to the runtime-serving connection (no unbounded buffering)
AbortSignal integration: aborting the ReadableStream/AsyncIterator triggers underlying request cancellation and resolves outstanding promises cleanly
Retries: when client-side transient retry triggers, adapters do not duplicate emitted tokens and re-establish stream continuation using server-provided resume token where available
Comprehensive examples added under examples/ts: Next.js edge, Deno edge function, Node 20 worker and server, with CI smoke tests
Documentation page describing ergonomics, migration steps from streamBridge(), and compatibility matrix
No new runtime-only surface leaked to public API; surface is purely adapter/factory-based and can be tree-shaken
implementation_notes: Introduce StreamConsumerFactory<TEvent> with methods: toAsyncIterable(), toWebStream(), toNodeStream(options?)
Internally implement a single hub that normalizes transport frames into canonical events and supports tee() for multiple views without duplicating network reads
Use built-in ReadableStream controller strategy for backpressure in browsers and node:Readable.toWeb / stream.Readable.from where possible
Implement a small polyfill shim for environments lacking ReadableStream.from (Deno older versions) guarded by feature-detects
Retry semantics: expose optional resumeToken produced by server; when retrying, use resume token and perform idempotent continuation rather than re-reading initial bytes
Type-level: Event generics: StreamEvent<Data> | StreamEvent<Done> | StreamEvent<Error>; prefer discriminated unions so consumers can narrow with event.type
Expose helper utilities: collectToString(asyncIterator), pipeToWritable(stream, writable), drainWithTimeout for tests
Ensure method names are stable: avoid introducing streamBridge() replacement until deprecation cycle completed
Performance: avoid micro-allocations per token; reuse frame objects internally and copy only when crossing public boundary
test_plan: Unit tests for adapters: toAsyncIterable(), toWebStream(), toNodeStream() in Node 18+ and Node 20
Integration smoke for Next.js Edge example using @vercel/edge-runtime local runner
Backpressure test: consumer reads slowly (100ms delay) and assert that underlying socket does not buffer more than N chunks (configurable)
Abort semantics test: abort signal mid-stream and assert cancellation propagated to fetch and no dangling promises
Retry test: force transient 503 on first attempt, ensure resume token used and client continues from correct token without duplication
Type tests using tsd to validate exported types and narrowing behaviors
Add CI job 'sdk-ts-streaming-smoke' that runs in node:20 image and Deno:1.35 image
rollout: Plan: land feature behind experimental flag `enableUnifiedStreams` in sdk-ts-3.4.0-canary. Collect telemetry for three weeks (errors, aborted streams, retry counts). After stability, flip flag in 3.4.0 stable and publish migration guide and deprecation notes for old helpers.
comments: 2026-03-03 Diego Ramos: Initial draft — outlined the problem and high-level factory approach. Assigned to Amina for design/impl pairing.
2026-03-05 Amina Patel: Prototype of toAsyncIterable() implemented. Noticed Node 18's stream.Readable.from produces different highWaterMark behavior; added backpressure tests to plan.

2026-03-07 Priya Singh (Review): Typing looks good but suggest exposing a small 'eventsOnly' option for consumers that only want data tokens to avoid union narrowing boilerplate. Also asked to ensure examples include both token-level and stringified outputs.
2026-03-09 Samir Gupta (Security): Quick review — no secrets persisted; ensure AbortSignal cancellation cancels any credentials refresh. Marked security_review_required=false.
2026-03-11 Amina Patel: Implemented tee-based multi-view internally; added Deno polyfill detection. Created draft PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/redwood-sdk/pull/2123
2026-03-12 QA: Found flaky test in backpressure scenario when Node event-loop starving; added small throttle util and increased default highWaterMark in test harness.
notes: Because streaming is a core SDK primitive, any typing/API churn must be narrowly scoped and accompanied by clear migration examples. Keep experimental flag in place until we have 50k+ hours of CI run-time across example workloads. Consider telemetry knobs to sample token sizes and average emitted-per-second for early detection of regressions.
